app.title: Ocean Foundry
param.ocean.width.label: Width (X)
param.ocean.width.help: How many blocks the water covers from west to east, along the X axis.
param.ocean.length.label: Length (Z)
param.ocean.length.help: How many blocks the water covers from north to south, along the Z axis.
param.ocean.placement_y.label: Placement Y
param.ocean.placement_y.help: The Minecraft Y level the water rests at. This is the average level: crests rise above it and troughs dip below it.
param.ocean.wave_height.label: Wave height
param.ocean.wave_height.help: Height in blocks of the tallest waves, from trough to crest. Individual waves vary, so most are smaller than this.
param.ocean.peak_distance.label: Peak distance
param.ocean.peak_distance.help: Typical distance in blocks from one main crest to the next. Real spacing varies around this value.
param.ocean.direction.label: Wave direction
param.ocean.direction.help: The way the waves face, in degrees. 0° points east (+X) and 90° points south (+Z).
param.ocean.irregularity.label: Irregularity
param.ocean.irregularity.help: How uneven the waves are. Low values give regular rows; high values give mixed heights, uneven spacing and broken crest lines.
param.ocean.swell_detail.label: Swell detail
param.ocean.swell_detail.help: How much smaller swell rides between the main waves. This shapes the concrete; fine ripples are added by shading instead.
param.ocean.crest_sharpness.label: Crest sharpness
param.ocean.crest_sharpness.help: Low values give rounded, rolling crests. High values give narrow peaks with wide, flat troughs.
param.ocean.seed.label: Shape seed
param.ocean.seed.help: A number that fixes the arrangement of waves. The same seed always gives the same shape. Randomise tries a different arrangement.
param.ocean.build_style.label: Build style
param.ocean.build_style.help: Hollow shell builds only a layer that follows the surface. Filled builds solid concrete from the surface down to a flat base.
param.ocean.shell_thickness.label: Shell thickness
param.ocean.shell_thickness.help: How many blocks thick the hollow shell is. Only used with the hollow shell style.
param.ocean.foundation_colour.label: Foundation concrete
param.ocean.foundation_colour.help: The concrete colour used for the foundation underneath the coloured surface. It shows through wherever glass and coating are left off.
param.ocean.include_colour_glass.label: Include colour and glass
param.ocean.include_colour_glass.help: When off, only the concrete foundation is built, with no coloured surface and no stained glass.
param.ocean.metres_per_block.label: Metres per block
param.ocean.metres_per_block.help: The real-world size one block stands for. It sets how fast the waves are for their size, and so how strongly a current acts on them: with smaller blocks the same current leaves a longer, taller wake.
param.ocean.flow_speed.label: Current speed
param.ocean.flow_speed.help: How fast the sea runs past the land, in metres a second. The water piles up against land in its way and leaves a wake of standing waves and white water behind it. 0 gives no current. It only shows around land or a build.
param.ocean.flow_direction.label: Current direction
param.ocean.flow_direction.help: The way the current runs, in degrees. 0° runs east (+X) and 90° runs south (+Z).
param.ocean.impact_foam.label: Collision white water
param.ocean.impact_foam.help: How much white water the current throws up where it strikes land, and how hard the waves it raises break on that shore. 0 leaves none, 1 the most; a faster current raises bigger ones. Only shows while the current runs.
param.ocean.wake_foam.label: Trailing white water
param.ocean.wake_foam.help: How much foam the current drags away downstream from land. 0 leaves none, 1 leaves the most. It always breaks up as it goes, so it never covers the sea in a solid sheet.
param.ocean.wake_length.label: Trail length
param.ocean.wake_length.help: How far downstream the trailing foam is drawn out. 1 is normal, 0 ends it right behind the land, 3 draws a long thin trail. A longer trail is fainter, since the same foam is spread thinner.
param.ocean.wake_scale.label: Wake size
param.ocean.wake_scale.help: How big the trail of white water reads: how far it is drawn out and how wide it fans out to the sides. 1 is normal. It multiplies the trail length, so 3 reaches three times as far and spreads wider on the way; below 1 tucks the trail in close behind the land.
param.ocean.spray.label: Spray
param.ocean.spray.help: How high a breaking wave throws its white water as it meets the shore. 0 keeps the white water on the surface, 1 throws it two or three blocks up along the rock. Bigger waves and a faster current throw more.
param.lava.width.label: Width (X)
param.lava.width.help: How many blocks the lava covers from west to east, along the X axis.
param.lava.length.label: Length (Z)
param.lava.length.help: How many blocks the lava covers from north to south, along the Z axis.
param.lava.placement_y.label: Placement Y
param.lava.placement_y.help: The Minecraft Y level the lava surface rests at.
param.lava.map_scale.label: Pattern scale
param.lava.map_scale.help: How many blocks one repeat of the lava pattern covers. Larger values give bigger plates and wider cracks.
param.lava.rotation.label: Pattern rotation
param.lava.rotation.help: Turns the lava pattern relative to the foundation, in degrees.
param.lava.seed.label: Pattern seed
param.lava.seed.help: A number that fixes the arrangement of the lava pattern. The same seed always gives the same result.
param.lava.flow_distortion.label: Flow distortion
param.lava.flow_distortion.help: Bends the pattern as if the lava were slowly flowing. Zero leaves the pattern undistorted.
param.lava.crust_coverage.label: Crust coverage
param.lava.crust_coverage.help: How much of the surface is cooled, dark crust. Low values leave mostly molten lava showing.
param.lava.glow.label: Baked glow
param.lava.glow.help: How bright the hot regions are painted. This only changes block colours; it does not create real Minecraft light.
param.lava.interpretation.label: Read pattern as
param.lava.interpretation.help: Slope puts heat on steep parts of the pattern. Fissures puts heat in the valleys, like cracks between cooled plates.

param.ocean.dark_colour.label: Dark colour
param.ocean.dark_colour.help: The colour of the water where little light reaches it: faces turned away from the sun, deep troughs, shadows, and the whole sea when there is no sunlight. Any colour you like, black included. The blocks pass from this colour to the light colour by themselves.
param.ocean.light_colour.label: Light colour
param.ocean.light_colour.help: The colour of the water where the light catches it: faces turned to the sun, thin crests and sunlit shallows. Level water lies about half way between the two colours. Reflections take a paler tint of this colour unless they are given one of their own.
param.ocean.lit_strength.label: Sunlight
param.ocean.lit_strength.help: How much direct sun reaches the water. At 0 the sky is fully overcast and the whole sea takes the dark colour; the more sun, the further the water goes toward the light colour.
param.ocean.depth_influence.label: Shallow lightening
param.ocean.depth_influence.help: How much paler the water is where it is shallow. It only has an effect where there is terrain under the water.
param.ocean.depth_reach.label: Shallow depth
param.ocean.depth_reach.help: Water shallower than this many blocks counts as shallow: it is lightened and lets the sea floor show. The effect is strongest at the shore and gone at this depth.
param.ocean.foam_amount.label: Foam amount
param.ocean.foam_amount.help: How much white water there is: whitecaps on breaking crests, and foam where the sea meets land. 0 gives none.
param.ocean.foam_streaks.label: Storm foam
param.ocean.foam_streaks.help: Extra white water on tall waves: more breaking crests, foam lace behind them and streaks drawn out by the wind. 0 gives none.
param.ocean.shading_strength.label: Wave shading
param.ocean.shading_strength.help: How much the colour changes across a wave. The direction of the sun leads: faces turned to it are lighter, faces turned away darker. Thin crests are a little paler and deep troughs a little darker as well. Under cloud the sky shades the waves instead, more gently. 0 colours the sea evenly. The shape itself is already shaded by the game, so this does not need to be strong.
param.ocean.contrast.label: Shading contrast
param.ocean.contrast.help: How quickly the colour goes from the shaded side of a wave to the sunlit side. Higher values give harder edges between dark and light water.
param.ocean.light_bearing.label: Sun direction
param.ocean.light_bearing.help: The direction the sunlight comes from. 0° is east (+X) and 90° is south (+Z), the same as the wave direction.
param.ocean.light_elevation.label: Sun height
param.ocean.light_elevation.help: How high the sun stands above the horizon. A low sun throws long shadows behind cliffs and tall waves; a high sun lights the sea evenly.
param.ocean.ripple_strength.label: Ripple shading
param.ocean.ripple_strength.help: Fine ripples too small to build, added to the colour only. They break up large areas of a single colour and scatter the glints of the sun.
param.ocean.reflection_auto.label: Reflections take the light colour
param.ocean.reflection_auto.help: When on, reflections are a paler tint of the light colour, so two colours describe the whole sea. Turn it off to give reflections a colour of their own, such as grey under a clouded sky.
param.ocean.daylight.label: Daylight
param.ocean.daylight.help: How much light there is in all. Lower it for dusk, heavy cloud or night: the water darkens, and the foam and the reflections with it, though less. At 0 the water is black. How dark the sea is depends only on these colour settings, never on the size of the waves.
param.ocean.clarity.label: Water clarity
param.ocean.clarity.help: How clearly the sea floor shows through shallow water. 0 hides it; higher values let the sand or rock beneath tint the water near the shore.
param.ocean.shade_midpoint.label: Level water
param.ocean.shade_midpoint.help: Where level water in full sun sits between the dark colour and the light colour. At one half it is half way; lower makes the whole sea darker, higher makes it lighter.
param.ocean.shadow_strength.label: Shadows
param.ocean.shadow_strength.help: How dark the shadows are that land, arches and tall waves cast on the water. 0 gives none.
param.ocean.shadow_softness.label: Shadow softness
param.ocean.shadow_softness.help: How soft the edges of those shadows are, in blocks.
param.ocean.reflection_strength.label: Reflections
param.ocean.reflection_strength.help: How much light the surface throws back without it entering the water: glints of the sun and the sheen of the sky. 0 gives none.
param.ocean.reflection_colour.label: Reflection colour
param.ocean.reflection_colour.help: The colour of the sky and sun as the water mirrors them: pale blue-white on a clear day, grey under cloud.
param.ocean.reflection_softness.label: Glint spread
param.ocean.reflection_softness.help: How widely the glints of the sun spread. Low values give a few sharp sparkles on the steepest faces; high values a broad, soft shine.
param.ocean.view_elevation.label: Viewing height
param.ocean.view_elevation.help: A reflection depends on where it is seen from, and a build is seen from everywhere, so one onlooker is assumed. This is how high they look down from. 90° is straight above, as on a map, and gives only sparkles; lower angles add the pale sheen of the sky on slopes facing away from them.
param.ocean.view_bearing.label: Viewing direction
param.ocean.view_bearing.help: The side the assumed onlooker stands on. 0° is east (+X) and 90° is south (+Z), the same as the wave direction.
param.ocean.glass_layers.label: Glass layers
param.ocean.glass_layers.help: How many layers of stained glass lie over the coloured surface. With 2 or 3, the layers blend the borders between block colours. 0 builds no glass.
param.ocean.max_solids.label: Solid block types
param.ocean.max_solids.help: The most kinds of solid coloured block the surface may use. Fewer kinds are easier to gather; more give smoother colour.
param.ocean.max_glass.label: Glass colours
param.ocean.max_glass.help: The most colours of stained glass the build may use.
param.ocean.dither_strength.label: Dithering
param.ocean.dither_strength.help: Mixes neighbouring block colours in a fine pattern, so the steps between them are harder to see. 0 gives clean bands.

file.open.help: Open a Litematica, WorldEdit or Axiom file to see what is in it and save it in another format. The original file is never changed.
file.explain.omit_air.help: Only real blocks are written, as a set of boxes with no air in them. Pasting can never remove anything from your world, whatever Litematica's settings are. All the boxes belong to one placement: move and paste them together, not one at a time.
file.explain.compact.help: The file keeps its air blocks. So that pasting does not carve air into your world, set Litematica's "Paste replace behavior" to "None" or "With non-air" before pasting.
file.explain.no_air.help: This build contains no air blocks, so pasting cannot remove anything from your world.
file.explain.sponge.help: A WorldEdit file is one solid box, so empty space is saved as air. Paste with //paste -a so the air is skipped and your world is not carved out.
file.explain.axiom.help: Axiom blueprints do not store empty space, so nothing is written where the build has no block.
action.export.help: Save the baked ocean as a file you can paste into your world.
tuning.title.help: The generator's internal numbers are kept in a text file while the method is still being developed. Change a number, save the file and bake again. Delete the file to get the defaults back.
tuning.updated.help: The generator's method has changed since your tuning file was written, so the file was replaced with the new defaults. Your old numbers are kept in {file}.
panel.advanced.help: Things seldom needed: for now, the file of numbers behind the generator.
mode.ocean.help: Build a sea: waves, colour, foam and glass.
mode.lava.help: Lava surfaces: cooled crust, molten cracks and glow.
action.files.help: Open a Litematica, WorldEdit or Axiom file, see what is in it and save it in another format.
action.cancel.help: Stop this job. The previous result is kept.
status.help: Whether the build on screen matches the settings.
compute.help: The device doing the calculating. Click to choose another.
compute.auto.help: Use the fastest device that passed the check.
compute.cpu.help: Calculate on the processor only. Slower, but it works on every computer.
viewport.layers.no_glass.help: Hide the stained glass to see the coloured surface under it.
viewport.blocks.help: Every kind of block in the build and how many of each. Click to fold the list away.
export.part.help: Save the whole build, or one part of it to paste on its own.
file.format.sponge.help: For WorldEdit and most other building tools.
file.omit_air.help: Write only real blocks, as boxes with no air in them, so pasting can never remove anything from your world.
file.save.help: Choose where to save the file.
scene.title.help: The land the sea is baked around, and the rivers and waterfalls on it: a test land, or a build of your own.
scene.land.coast.help: A test coast: a beach that turns into a cliff sea front, and an island with a beach and rocky shores.
scene.land.cliffs.help: A test cliff coast: a headland with a rock arch, rocks standing in the sea, a shingle bay, and a stream that falls into a cove.
scene.land.build.help: A build file of your own standing in the sea. The waves, the foam and the current shape themselves around it.
scene.build.file.help: The build that stands in the sea. Litematic, Sponge schematic, Axiom blueprint and older schematic files can be read. It is placed block for block; a hollow build is closed to the sea.
scene.build.waterline.help: How far up the build the water rests, as a share of its height. 0 stands the build on the water; 0.2 puts the lowest fifth of it under water.
scene.build.offset.help: The build stands in the middle of the sea. These numbers move it east and south, in blocks; negative numbers move it west and north.
scene.build.map.help: North is up. Grey is where the build stands in the water or hangs over it. The colour along its edge shows the kind of shore the sea meets there.
scene.map.help: North is up. Drag the dots to place a river: the white dot is where it rises, the coloured dot where it is headed. It runs downhill, becomes a waterfall wherever the ground drops away, and ends where it meets the sea. The colours along the shore show what kind of shore the land makes there. The circles are calm water and keep-dry areas; drag their dots to move them.
scene.shore.delta.help: A low beach with shallow water in front, where a river can build a delta.
scene.shore.rocky.help: Waves break up among the rocks.
scene.shore.cliff.help: Waves are thrown back by it.
scene.add_river.help: Add another river, then drag its dots on the map.
scene.add_river.full: Twelve rivers is the most a land can hold.
scene.pond.help: Still water in a hollow of the land. Drag its square on the map into the hollow.
scene.add_pond.help: Add a pond, then drag its square on the map into a hollow.
scene.add_pond.full: Twelve ponds is the most a land can hold.
scene.open.map.help: North is up. The circles are calm water and keep-dry areas; drag their dots to move them.
scene.zone.calm.help: Smaller waves and less foam inside the circle, easing back to the open sea at its edge.
scene.zone.dry.help: No water inside the circle, to leave room for a build.
scene.zone.radius.help: How far the area reaches from its middle, in blocks.
scene.zone.strength.help: How much of the waves is taken away in the middle: 0 leaves them, 1 leaves the water flat.
scene.add_calm.help: Add a circle of calmer water, as in a harbour, then drag its dot on the map.
scene.add_dry.help: Add a circle left without water, then drag its dot on the map.
scene.add_zone.full: Twelve areas is the most a scene can hold.
scene.pond.depth.help: How deep the water stands over the lowest point of the hollow, in blocks.
scene.pond.dig.help: Digs a round basin this many blocks out from the square, so the pond holds water even on a slope. 0 fills only a hollow the land already has.
scene.pond.dry: In the sea, not on the land
scene.pond.none: No hollow here: the water runs away
scene.pond.spills.sea: Spills into the sea at {depth} of {asked} blocks deep
scene.pond.spills.edge: Runs off the edge of the plot at {depth} of {asked} blocks deep
scene.pond.spills.river: Runs into a river at {depth} of {asked} blocks deep
scene.pond.spills.help: The hollow is shallower than asked. The water stands at the lowest point of its rim. Move the square or lower the depth.
scene.width.help: How wide the river is, in blocks.
scene.winding.help: How much the river wanders on its way down. At 0 it runs as straight as the ground allows.
scene.delta.help: How large a delta the river builds where it meets the sea. 0 gives none. A delta needs a low beach with shallow water in front.
scene.seed.help: A number that fixes the shape of the land. Another number gives another land of the same kind.
tuning.folder.help: Show the file in its folder: {file}
tuning.reset.help: Write the default numbers again. The ones replaced are kept in {file}.
param.ocean.moment.label: Moment
param.ocean.moment.help: Moves the same sea on in time; every wave travels at its own speed. One step is the time the main wave takes to pass.
param.ocean.swell_height.label: Swell height
param.ocean.swell_height.help: A long, even swell from a storm far away, under the waves the wind raises here. Its height from trough to crest, in blocks. 0 gives none.
param.ocean.swell_length.label: Swell length
param.ocean.swell_length.help: The distance between two swell crests, in blocks.
param.ocean.swell_direction.label: Swell direction
param.ocean.swell_direction.help: The way the swell travels, in degrees. 0° runs east (+X) and 90° runs south (+Z).
param.ocean.foam_colour.label: Foam colour
param.ocean.dither_mode.label: Dither pattern
param.ocean.dither_mode.help: How two block colours are mixed where one changes into the next. Patches are a few blocks across and drawn out along the crests. Ordered is a fixed fine pattern, Scattered is random, Error diffusion passes on what each block could not show. None gives clean bands.
param.ocean.dither_grain.label: Dither grain
param.ocean.dither_grain.help: How many blocks across one cell of the pattern is. Larger values give a coarser mix.
param.ocean.dither_seed.label: Dither seed
param.ocean.dither_seed.help: A number that fixes the scatter. The same seed always gives the same scatter.
param.lava.pattern.label: Pattern
param.lava.pattern.help: The kind of lava surface: cooled plates with glowing cracks, folded ropes, or molten pools.
param.lava.invert.label: Invert pattern
param.lava.invert.help: Swaps the hot and the cooled parts of the pattern.
param.lava.crust_colour.label: Crust colour
param.lava.crust_colour.help: The colour of the cooled crust.
param.lava.molten_colour.label: Molten colour
param.lava.molten_colour.help: The colour of the molten lava between the crust and the hottest parts.
param.lava.hot_colour.label: Hottest colour
param.lava.hot_colour.help: The colour of the hottest lava.
param.lava.relief.label: Relief
param.lava.relief.help: How many blocks the crust stands above the molten parts. 0 builds a flat surface.
param.lava.foundation_colour.label: Foundation concrete
param.lava.foundation_colour.help: The concrete colour used for the foundation underneath the coloured surface.
param.lava.glass_layers.label: Glass layers
param.lava.glass_layers.help: How many layers of stained glass lie over the coloured surface. 0 builds no glass.
param.lava.max_solids.label: Solid block types
param.lava.max_solids.help: The most kinds of solid coloured block the surface may use.
param.lava.max_glass.label: Glass colours
param.lava.max_glass.help: The most colours of stained glass the build may use.
param.lava.dither_strength.label: Dithering
param.lava.dither_strength.help: Mixes neighbouring block colours in a fine pattern, so the steps between them are harder to see. 0 gives clean bands.
viewport.show.wanted.help: A map of the colour the surface asks for, before blocks are chosen.
viewport.show.blocks.help: A map of the colour the chosen blocks give.
viewport.show.difference.help: A map of how far the block colour is from the wanted colour. Brighter is further.
viewport.show.height.help: A map of the surface height. Lighter is higher.
viewport.blocks.exclude: Click to leave this block out of the next bake.
viewport.blocks.restore: Click to allow these blocks again:
project.menu.help: Project files, profiles and the last few bakes.
project.open.help: Open a project file: its mode, every setting, the blocks left out and the land.
project.save.help: Save the mode, every setting, the blocks left out and the land in a project file.
project.profiles.help: Looks kept under a name in the data folder.
project.profile.name: Profile name
project.profile.save.help: Keep the current settings as a profile under this name.
project.history.help: The settings of the last five bakes.
project.history.missing: There is no past bake number {n}.
project.history.item.help: Bring back the settings of this bake.
status.estimate.help: About how many blocks the next bake will make and how long it will take, going by the last one.
param.ocean.pattern_source.label: Ripples from
param.ocean.pattern_source.help: Where the fine shading ripples come from: the wind's own, a pattern from the library, a wave spectrum, or a normal map image chosen in the scene card.
param.ocean.pattern_name.label: Pattern
param.ocean.pattern_name.help: The library pattern used for the ripples.
param.ocean.pattern_spread.label: Direction spread
param.ocean.pattern_spread.help: How widely the ripples' directions fan out around the main one. 0 sends them all one way.
param.ocean.pattern_peak.label: Peak sharpness
param.ocean.pattern_peak.help: How much the ripples gather around one size. Higher gives more regular, even rows.
param.ocean.pattern_span.label: Pattern size
param.ocean.pattern_span.help: Blocks one tile of the pattern covers. Its shape is kept.
param.ocean.pattern_strength.label: Pattern strength
param.ocean.pattern_strength.help: How strongly the pattern tilts the shading, on top of Ripple shading.
param.ocean.pattern_rotation.label: Pattern turn
param.ocean.pattern_rotation.help: Turns the pattern away from the wave direction, in degrees.
param.ocean.pattern_invert.label: Invert pattern
param.ocean.pattern_invert.help: Turns the pattern's hills into hollows.
param.ocean.pattern_flip_y.label: Green channel
param.ocean.pattern_flip_y.help: Which way the image's green channel points. Auto reads it from the image. A grey image is read as heights.
param.ocean.seabed.label: Imagined sea floor
param.ocean.seabed.help: For open sea with no land: a sea floor that only changes how deep the water looks and where waves break. No blocks are added.
param.ocean.seabed_shallowest.label: Shallowest depth
param.ocean.seabed_shallowest.help: Depth in blocks at the shallow edge of the plot.
param.ocean.seabed_slope.label: Floor slope
param.ocean.seabed_slope.help: Blocks deeper for every block out from the shallow edge.
param.ocean.seabed_direction.label: Deepens toward
param.ocean.seabed_direction.help: The way the floor falls away, in degrees as for the waves.
param.ocean.creative_blocks.label: Creative-only blocks
param.ocean.creative_blocks.help: Also use blocks that can only be had in creative mode.
viewport.layers.surface.help: Show only the coloured top blocks.
viewport.layers.glass.help: Show only the stained glass over the water.
viewport.show.depth.help: A map of the water depth. Lighter is shallower.
viewport.show.foam.help: A map of the white water. White is foam.
viewport.show.normals.help: Which way the built surface faces, coloured as a normal map.
viewport.show.reflection.help: A map of how much of the colour is mirrored sky. Lighter is more.
viewport.cutaway.help: Leave out everything east of the slider, to see inside the build.
scene.pattern.file.help: The normal map or grey height map the ripples are taken from. It is mirrored to tile without seams.
scene.pattern.choose.help: Pick a PNG or JPEG image.
scene.pattern.none: No image chosen: the wind's ripples are used.
scene.pattern.unreadable: Can't read this image: the wind's ripples are used.
export.area.help: Save only the blocks inside the edges below, at their places in the plot.
export.area.west.help: West edge, in blocks from the plot's west side.
export.area.north.help: North edge, in blocks from the plot's north side.
export.area.east.help: East edge, in blocks from the plot's west side.
export.area.map.help: Drag across the map to mark the area to save.
export.area.south.help: South edge, in blocks from the plot's north side.
